utterances.text: [Interpretation] Normally speaking, you must put your questions during the cross-examination, please. So this question is a question we will get back to at a later stage. But this was a relevant comment. Could the witness tell us where he was standing and where his friend fell. I did see the picture, but I would know -- like to know exactly where the victim was standing and where --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just ask.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I will do that, Your Honour, and the witness may be able to assist us. I will also indicate that there is other additional evidence coming by video - not this photograph but a video - by which the witness -- a witness has marked the location on the street, and you'll have that in the course of the evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Pejanovic, if you can, please, answer the President -- Mr. -- the President's question. Looking at this photograph, and you may not have exactly the right vantage point, but can you tell us as much as you can where you were and where Mr. Jugo was when you saw him lying -- I think you said he -- at one point he was resting on an elbow, where he was located at that time. If we can move the picture -- if you want us to move the picture in one direction or the other, just please say so.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Back a bit, please. Move the picture back a bit. Stop. Fine. A moment ago, you saw the edge of the wall. So between one and a half and two metres away from that was the edge of the water truck. And if you take it that the vehicle was about 1 metre, 80 centimetres wide, it was a wide truck, then that would make the truck come up at the edge of the pavement where this sign is, saying "Prodavnica." He was moving towards the edge of the pavement. He opened the door to the back part of the car or water truck, because the cabin was in front and they kept the equipment underneath the front seat, and the -- what the -- the equipment they used to pump up the tyres. At that moment when he put down his equipment underneath the seat and went back to close the door, at that very moment I heard a scream and he says, "Oh, mother." I was standing on the opposite side. If we go back a bit again, I will show you where I was standing. That's right. Roughly somewhere there, the edge of the wall, because I was coming from the office, which is right behind this wall. Because I told our female colleague to make us some coffee. I had just stepped outside. I had been -- I was away from the wall some 50 centimetres or a metre, facing the water truck. So I was opposite the door to the vehicle where he was hit and where he fell. And it was his left knee and left elbow that he was leaning against. And he tried to -- he managed to come out to the front part of the vehicle so that we were not in danger and so that we could pick him up and take him away from the spot, which is what we did. I know that when I took him to hospital or, rather, when he was put up in hospital, the people there said that it was somewhere below the right breast from the outside, from the back, that is, that he was hit somewhere below the right breast, his right nipple, and that the exit wound was there. I'd like to stress once again I'm not a strategist myself, strategic expert. I'm not a soldier. But they said that the bullet that hit him was called a bone cracker and that it cut through his internal organs, his diaphragm and liver, and that in fact he died as a result of the bleeding, the internal bleeding. We gave him six bottles of blood, blood transfusion over a period of 24 hours. I came to visit him towards evening. He was in a coma. He wasn't conscious of anything. I went back again in the morning. He was sweating, in a very poor state, completely pale, and the doctors told me there was very little likelihood of him surviving. But there you are, we always lived in the hope of surviving. And as I say, he held out for 24 hours after the incident, and then expired.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Pejanovic, in reference to the photograph that's on the screen now, do I understand your testimony correctly that then Mr. Jugo would have been on the street side. You have the building on the photograph to the right, and then you have the street side on the left. Mr. Jugo was on the street side of the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That's quite true. And that's how it would have been, because when he opened the door to where you get in and sit down, then that whole -- he had to come out for that whole width of the door. He had to step beyond the pavement into the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, could I ask you to -- we'll pan the photograph further around. I don't know if we ever got to the point of identifying the Razvitak building or not, but would you please tell us when you see the Razvitak building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you stop the image. One technical detail. The Prosecution failed to think of this. Witness, you say that he was hit by a bullet. Was it a single shot, or were there several shots, one of which hit him in the back? Did you hear the noise made by the shot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One. And that one was fatal. It set his destiny.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, was he -- was he there, I mean, on the photo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. That building, Razvitak, was built towards the end of the 1970s.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, how can you account for the fact that he could be hit -- the victim could be hit by a bullet whilst with the angle of the shot and this building it would be difficult for him to be hit by a bullet, because you have this high building just across the road where, according to you, the one who shot the shot was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour -- the witness can certainly answer. I think there's a misunderstanding as to why the significance of this location.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Pejanovic, can you please answer the President's question as best you can as to where you understood the shot came from that killed Mr. Jugo.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Stop. The bullet had to come from the opposite side, from the western part of town. My assumption is that it was somewhere near the nowadays Spanish Square. Can we take the footage back? Can I see the corner of the street, please? Can you rewind a bit, and I will show you the location where eight people were wounded in their arms, legs, or below their collarbones. Stop. Sir, look to the upper left corner. You see a blue facade there, next to the traffic light. One metre away from this curve is a location where eight people were injured. One of the eight was my colleague Cedo. A bullet hit him just below his collarbone and exited below his shoulder. In other cases, that of Refik Saric, he was coming back from the hospital, the war hospital, which is located close to this corner, some 30 to 40 metres away. So coming back from the hospital where he had visited his wounded son - he was wounded at the front - he was hit by a sniper in his arm or hand. He had gloves on, and the bullet went through his gloves. This is how he came to our premises. Another five people were lightly wounded by a sniper in that location. I assume, but I cannot be certain of this, that somewhere near Spanish Square there had to be either some kind of a platform or a location from which they could have easily climbed the trees and fire and then quickly come down. The sniper was never discovered. Both sides used snipers, because they targeted each other. This was widely known. And this particular sniper was never discovered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we're lucky to have this 360-degree photo. Could you not identify the place where this sniper was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It would be hard, because it was on the other side, not in the vicinity. Rather, it's not very far, but it's the other side, across the bridge, behind the Bristol Hotel. I think somewhere near Spanish Square. If you look at this map, I can show you where Spanish Square is and then you can see how far we were from that location, and you will be able to see that it was very easy to fire from there. For a long time there was a sniper location on the Privredna bank building. There was a sniper there for a long time, and he had a great view, because that was high enough so he would have a great view across the Tito's bridge to our premises. And there in Hrasnica, five people were injured, out of which three were killed. The situation was such that we didn't dare approach a person who was wounded because it would be risky to us. And we would simply throw a rope, and if the person had enough strength, we would pull him out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may assist. The witness just referred to -- which is what I was going to take the witness back to the map, Exhibit P09517, which we've been looking at today. And if that could be placed -- if we can also have that on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, to re-orient -- excuse me, re-orient us, sir, could you show us again the location of the fire station, which I believe you marked this morning as position number 1. Can you find your mark number 1 and point to that, please.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's right here. There is a circle and number 1. And then across is a rectangle and number 2. This is the Razvitak department store.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So the photograph that we're looking at, is it correct, is of the street and when we look down the street, it's the street running between location number 1 and location number 2; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is called -- this street is called Brkica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, looking back to the map again, and we're going to have to go back and forth here for a moment, can you indicate -- can you show by your pencil where that street crosses the Neretva River and where it goes into West Mostar, and would you stop when you get to Spanish Square.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Starting from this location where we just now were, where we're located, this would be the direction taken. And then this takes us to Spanish Square. There are two possibilities. One is this: There is a street called Drinski Street, and then in continuation there is Hrasnica and then Safeta Mujica Street, and the other one is Ante Zuanica [phoen]. So there in the corner there was the Privredna bank building, known as Glas Bank in Mostar. So one possibility is that from that facility, this is where the bullet came from, and the other possibility was that in Zrinjski Street there was a platform from which they could easily climb up and then come down and go away. So the platform option is my assumption. As for the bank building, it's a fact that there was a small house from which a sniper used to shoot.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, if we could go back to the photograph, the 360-degree photograph, please. Now, when you look up in the street in the direction -- in the street going away from us, for the purposes of the record, we're in the foreground by the Audi sign and the street is running away from us, which direction is that street going? Is that going towards Spanish Square and across the Neretva River, or going away from? Can you tell us, please.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Behind this sign, Audi car parts, if you go further away, that takes you to Spanish Square.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And Mr. Jugo was standing essentially in the street, on the street side of the vehicle at the time he was struck; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A question is going to be put by the Judge.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... and which this picture might provide, the picture we are looking at might provide the help. One can see hills in the background. Previously today you have been asked about positions of guns. Could these be the hills you've been talking about? One would be Hulet [phoen], if I have it in good memory, and the other Brkanovo, or is it not related?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please accept this: It's somewhat difficult to recognise the entire area from this angle, but let me tell you, it's not Brkanovo hill. You can only see the portion of Brkanovo hill which is above the roof tiles. And then there's a road, and then to the right of the road there's another elevation where nowadays TV transmitters are. This is where Mikuljaca Mount is, quite a large mountain. So to the right of this road is where Mikuljaca Mount begins. And to the left of this portion that's visible just above the roofs, this is where Hum hill is, and it's a distinct feature. One can see it well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Spanish Square, how far is it in relation to the truck? How far is it if we believe what you say, that there was a sniper between -- or on the Spanish Square? What is the distance from the Spanish Square to this location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, roughly speaking, I never actually considered this because there was no need for that, but if one took the road, it would be no more than 600 to 700 metres, maybe even less. And as the crow flies, it would be even less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this hill that you see in the background, how far would that be, according to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's quite a distance from this location. As far as I'm aware, the road taking to Brkanovo hill. One has to go to Balinovac and then take the road to Citluk and then turn right, so if one took the road, then it would be seven to 10 kilometres, roughly speaking. Of course, as the crow flies, much less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Scott. We needed these technical details. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Pejanovic, I think we've actually touched on another incident I want to direct your attention to where these five persons who were shot on the corner, then if we can just scan through the photograph again, I think you've already described that, but can you tell us -- can you stop us again where you say that these five persons -- where approximately five persons were shot by fire -- hit by fire.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Stop. On the frontal part of the photograph you see a red or dark red building. This is the library on the ground floor, and flats are above. To the right is a privately owned bakery. And where you see the entrance into the yard of the library, so starting from the edge of the bakery until the end where you see the traffic sign, this is the location where a lot of people were hit. I think that five of them were killed or wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Were any of your colleagues from the fire brigade wounded at that -- about this location?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: In this area, no, no. But to the beginning of the street -- if you can rotate the picture to the right, please. Stop there. All right. Well, right there, maybe one metre to metre and a half from the edge of this building as one went towards our facility my colleague Edo Dostovic was wounded. He's a member of the fire brigade to this day. And also Edo Saric was wounded. A bullet hit him on the arm as he was coming back from the hospital where he had visited his wounded son.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Pejanovic, so the record is clear, when you say "the edge of this building," there is a building on the far left edge of the photograph that I would say is a kind of light green. Is that the building you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's the building I have in mind. And as I said to you, from the edge and then further to the front some two metres or two and a half, I'm not sure, please don't hold me to this, it's hard to estimate. But as far as I remember, that's how it was. As soon as people emerged from behind the wall of the building, this would happen. I even have to say - I just remembered this - for a long time there on the wall there was a text saying, "Watch out for the sniper." And that was a warning for everybody, and it remained there until they renovated the facade of the building. This was a warning for everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And apart from Mr. Dostovic, did you have any other fire brigade colleagues who were killed and wounded at -- around this particular location?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: In this area, no, except for Dostovic. Riki Saric, my acquaintance and friend, he was hit in his arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, around this general -- this same location direction, around this Razvitak building, if we can pan back to the left, please -- excuse me, to the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I have a question to the record. On line 15, one speaks of an Edo Saric, and now on page 103, line 9, it is Riki Saric, and there is Edo Dostovic, I think. Maybe there has been a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could you clarify that, sir. You mentioned Mr. Dostovic and you did mention briefly, and my fault for not coming back to it, you mentioned another name. Are these two different individuals or have you confused the names of two different persons or are they separate incidents?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. These are two different persons, and I apologise to all of you if I misspoke. I'm trying to control what I'm saying as much as possible. It's possible that I misspoke. So first Edo Dostovic was wounded under his collarbone, and then Riki Saric was hit on his right arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And where was Mr. Saric located in reference to the photograph? We've now moved the photograph, but in reference to the location we were looking at previously.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Go back a bit, please. Stop. Right there. As I said, from this light green facade some two to two and a half metres away from the corner of the building towards the premises of the fire brigade. This is where both Edo and Riki were hit, as well as Emina Dedic and many others who were wounded there. Fortunately, none of them were killed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we can just pan a little bit more to the left. As we pan further to the left, then you come back to the fire -- just so we see where we are. Stop, please. This is coming back around to where the fire headquarters are located. Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And now if we can go back toward the Razvitak building -- excuse me, the Razvitak building. Can you -- can you tell the Judges, please, about any other sniping incident that took place in connection with the - excuse me - Razvitak building? If I can assist you by directing you to the 9th of May.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know roughly what it's about. This is the instance where the truck owned by Dervis Travnjak was hit. It was a light blue truck, and it was parked approximately just below this billboard, except that at the time there was no billboard there. So the building was parked roughly there. I was in the office together with a lady colleague of mine, and you could see where our offices were. It was -- they were right next to the pole, the electric pole. And then all of a sudden I heard several individual fire shots, and I thought that somebody was targeting the traffic sign, some of the snipers who had nothing better to do. The traffic sign had always been there, because this is the main road, and everybody coming from different roads have to yield. So I supposed that somebody was shooting at the traffic sign, and I went outside in front of our headquarters to see what was going on, and then I heard shots, and I saw that the sign was not hit. And when I looked better, I saw the truck was hit. I don't want to exaggerate, but I think seven to eight shots were fired towards the motor of the truck, and then four or five hit the windshield. And all of a sudden it occurred to me that they were trying to set the truck on fire. So they weren't really targeting the motor or anything like else, they were trying to set it on fire. And as I was thinking about that, I saw that the seats started -- the smoke started rising from the seats. And then I ran back into our headquarters, and one of my colleagues ran back to the truck. The truck was not locked. I mean, he wanted to do that, but I didn't allow him to run back to the truck and to move it from that location. And what was peculiar is that the sniper wasn't trying to target my colleague. My colleague came to the truck. He opened the door, and as I told you previously, we received a tank truck from our French colleagues which could carry 1.000 litres. And the water truck, we pulled it out just a little bit so that we could take the hose out - the hose was some 50 metres long - and we put out the fire or, rather, the seat that was smoking, and the shooting stopped. And then somebody went to inform the owner of the truck about what happened, and then as soon as it became dark, he moved the truck from there, and I don't know what happened afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have to have a break. It is now quarter to three. We shall resume at 3.00 for an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The hearing will now resume. Before I give the floor to Mr. Scott, Judge Trechsel has a question he would like to put to the witness. It concerns a technical matter.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Sorry. I would like to have some technical assistance in the sense that the picture be moved to the left until we have the view towards the west. No, the other direction, please. Yes. Now, we were told that the sniper shot most probably, I assume, more or less from the area around the P sign, the parking lot sign. I wonder whether it existed already at that time. And I wonder whether the witness could show us on this picture which windows he thinks could be the ones behind which the sniper was, or which rooftop. He has -- you have, sir, indicated certain locations. You have named them. But it would be helpful if we could also see them on this picture, because the distance makes the sniper story a bit delicate. So if you could show us. Thank you. I have just been instructed that there is no possibility on this video to actually technically apply a fingertip or a flesh -- an indicator, but perhaps you could describe.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, I will try to do that. I will go back to the map that we have. On the map, I pointed very clearly to the location of our headquarters, the position of the fire brigade, as well as the Spanish Square location. I have no other locations to point out to you. I showed you where our position was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It must be a misunderstanding. I was attentive when you spoke of the map and showed of the map, but we are now located, unless you tell me that I'm wrong, where the victim was standing, or crouching, when he was shot. Now, in sheer logic, from here you must see the place from where the sniper shot, and I would like to see this. I would like you to tell me what place this could be on the picture, not on the map. So perhaps by description. For instance, saying you take the top left angle of the blue parking sign and go up one centimetre, there seems to be a rooftop; in this way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I will be very clear, just like I was before. My position in relation to the victim was opposite. I was on the opposite side in view of the vehicle. From this location, there is nothing I can show you. I can show you nothing with my finger. You can't see the place from which this shooting came, because it is not on this picture. This is why I pointed you to the map. And on the map, I showed you the location of the Privredna bank building. And there, in the little elevator hut, there was an opening from which they fired. I told you that snipers from the opposite side tried to hit that sniper to put him out of action. The location that you are interested in is not on this photograph. It can only be shown to you on the map to show you where our location was and where the bank from which the sniper fired was located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry if I'm a bit insisting, but probably I've got something wrong, and I would like to be corrected. I thought that the position of the camera that takes this picture we see is practically identical to the position not where you were but where the victim who was shot at was, and normally a bullet goes in a straight line, which means that from the location of the victims - and this was not mortar shooting, it was a bullet - you are supposed to see the place where the bullet left the weapon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no theoretical chance for me to see that location, nor did I ever claim so. On the contrary, I said that I was on the right side, facing the front of the vehicle. So I was on the right of the vehicle, which was right next to the edge of the sidewalk. And as the driver opened the door of the vehicle to put equipment inside, whether he wanted it or not, he was basically left unprotected, standing in the street. And I don't know where the sniper was located, but he was in his view. I gave you two options where the sniper may have been located in the vicinity of Spanish Square, and it can only be seen, Spanish Square, on the map, not on this picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, it may assist, and particularly for Judge Trechsel, there will be -- there will be other witnesses who will talk about this particular incident and one who was closer to the actual spot than Mr. Pejanovic. So this will not be the only evidence on this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, in this same general area, before the break, before we leave this location, can you tell the Judges whether there was what -- what you believe to be a sniping incident when there were a large number of Muslim civilians gathered outside the Razvitak building? And can you describe that incident to the Judges, please.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Right now, or right at that moment where the truck was hit in front of the Razvitak building, is that what you have in mind? Do you mean the incident when the truck was targeted by a sniper?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, you told us about the time where the truck was hit, right before the break, and when there was an attempt, according to you, to set the truck on fire. Was there another incident - and if you don't recall, I'll move on - was there another incident where there were a large number of Muslim civilians gathered in the vicinity of the Razvitak building in which you believe a sniper shot was fired?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Please tell us.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: I remember that event. I'm sorry, I didn't immediately understand your question. I thought that you wanted some clarification about the previous incident. What happened on this occasion was this: After the 9th of May, when the conflict erupted, and then a week or two afterwards a compromise was reached and the shooting and shelling stopped. At one point they said that all of those who wanted to go back to their apartments in Western Mostar should go, report to their local communes and MUP and so on, and a lot of people followed that advice. And then at they started organising for the people to cross over to the right bank. It was done in an organised way. Nobody who was not recorded could cross to the other side. They had to put their names on a list first. If you take the camera angle a bit back, if you rewind this excerpt a little bit -- no, no, to the opposite side, please. Just a bit more. Stop here. Thank you. So here in this section behind the Razvitak building, I think that right there in that location there were about 1.000 to 1.500 people, prepared to go back because they had been told that an agreement had been reached and that they could go back to their homes. This was done in an organised way. People were boarding buses, private cars. Whoever had what, they were getting in and getting ready to cross to the other side. If you take the footage back a little bit, we need to see the zebra crossing, the pedestrian crossing. Thank you, that's fine. So as the people were boarding buses to go to the other bank, I stood there on the sidewalk a bit further away from this sign, which means I was able to see clearly how people were boarding buses, vehicles, and so on. And then, right then, a pigeon landed from the Razvitak building down there, and within a second or two it was shot by a sniper. And I don't think that a clearer message could have been sent to those who were trying to go back and with us boarding buses and cars and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention now, leaving -- leaving this photograph. Can you tell us, please, anything you know about the shooting of Mirzo Hamzic.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: A correction. There was no shooting at Mirzo Hamzic. It was the facility that was set fire to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apology. Please tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the morning, at around 5.30 a.m., we received a report according to which Mirzo Hamzic's house was on fire, and that is not far from our own premises, so it wasn't a great problem for us to approach the house. And when we got there, we saw that the roof was on fire. It's the general rule that you never approach a building on fire too close. You always park the truck a little further away. That's a tactical rule so that if the building is damaged and topples, the vehicle is not damaged. So we stopped at some 50 to 60 metres away from the house, and we tried to position our hose towards the building. While we were getting ready to do this and start putting out the fire, a sniper started shooting at us. While I was in the vehicle, sitting next to the driver, a sniper bullet shot past between the two of us and lodged in the seat. After that, there were a series of shots which hit the front part of our vehicle, the engine, the motor, in order to try and destroy it. Realising the situation we were facing, I said, "Let's all get out of the vehicle," because there were two other people, two other colleagues sitting behind us. We left the truck, got down from the truck, and the shooting did not cease. We were positioned right behind the vehicle. It was a TAP vehicle, 125, or T-10. I'm sorry. It was a T-10 type truck. But we weren't able to take shelter in somebody's house or yard and run across the road because of the sniper. While we were standing there behind the vehicle, we could just see the two front tyres which were pierced by sniper fire and the tyres went down. Three or four other rifle grenades were heard nearby, rifle launch grenades, and a man, Zezemi [phoen], told us to go into his house. We entered the house, and the rifle grenade gunfire continued. We were in the house with him and his wife. We had a cup of coffee, and after that we went outside and edged along the wall to get to our own premises. And then in the evening, we had to tow our truck off because there was no other way in which we could pull it out. Then we had to repair the tyres. Luckily, the motor wasn't too badly damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, can you look again at the map, Exhibit 9517, and can you mark -- find on that map and mark with the letter E the location that you were at, where the truck was located at this incident.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Opposite the street where it says, "Balaga," this is Cveci Street [phoen], the one to the left. Where the X is, the second street to the left. The first street is shorter. The second street is a little longer. It was at this street, at the bottom of the street. We were about 50 to 60 metres away from the building, as I said, so towards the end of the street. The building is right on the banks of the river Neretva. That's the location. What did you want me to place there, mark it how?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The letter E, please.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Done.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you at that time from your -- again from your knowledge of Mostar and this vicinity, did you have an understanding of where the shots were likely coming from?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: No dilemma there. I can tell you straight away. It could not have come from anywhere else but from the secondary school building called Aleksa Santic school.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you show us that location, please, on the map and mark it with the letter F.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where it says Spanish Square. So just off Spanish Square, 10 to 15 metres away. That was the location. That's where the secondary school building was. It was on the corner between Drinski Street and the Bulevar or, rather, the Spanish Square. It's back from -- it's some 10 metres back from the road, it's old building, and this is how it is positioned. It's a horseshoe shape. That's what it is. What, did you want F there? Did you want an F there?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Done, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is that location also known as the gymnasium?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The gymnasium, yes. Secondary school. And it's a secondary school to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to direct your attention next to an incident at a location called the Saric Harem. Can you tell us about that, please. And give us --

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You can start by giving us the approximate date of that incident.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: It was July. I know that full well. It was very hot. It was about 1.00 when we received the first information about the fire. I'll try here, where it says "port," there's an X, where Saric mosque is. So lower down from this X -- actually, the mosque is at the beginning of the Harem. So that's where it is. Where it says Luka, L-u-k-a, and I put X1, because the mosque was X, and this is X1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Can we -- can the ELMO be adjusted, please, so that we can see that. Up and to the right. Probably the opposite direction for you, perhaps. Yes. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Here you can see it. There's an X here. That's the mosque. But the mosque is at the start of the Harem, and it stretches this way, backwards, about 4 to 500 metres. That's the Harem area. We received this information about 1.00. We didn't go out on location straight away for several reasons. One of the main reasons was that at that point in time we didn't have a water truck ready, because the water trucks were already being used and had taken all the water. Second, to be quite frank, I never allowed, as leader of the unit, for two brothers or two relatives to go out on one assignment or to send people where I felt they would be unsafe and insecure. So I always waited, counted to 10, and then made my decisions, and that's what I did on that occasion as well. As luck would have it in this general situation, there was nothing to be burnt down in the Harem, just the stone, the stone and the wood and the graves; nothing particular. So waiting for a water truck to return and looking at tactics, generally speaking, we left some -- at about half past two. There were several calls coming in, saying that the flames were burning and spreading. We went to the location of the fire -- or, rather, we were at Marsal Tito Street, halfway -- I would say halfway down the Harem. We set up a hose channel, and some of my colleagues entered the Harem by edging against the wall. I stayed with the driver by the water truck. We had a radio station, communication, and we said we would only call if there was a burning need to do so. At one point in time, they managed to cover half the burning area and deal with half the area that was aflame. I was standing behind the water tank, at the valve, and I was grazed. I saw that it was a casing of -- a bullet casing that had grazed me. Just a surface graze and a little bleeding. While I was looking to see what had happened to me, the driver came up to me and said, "They're shooting at us again with a sniper." And I said, "Yes, and they just got me here," and I showed him where my arm had been grazed. All this happened in a split second. Then the shooting became continuous, and I said, "What shall we do?" And at that time my colleagues who were in the Harem called me and said, "What shall we do?" And I said, "Well, let's -- stay where you are, but try and withdraw and escape towards the mosque." I unbuttoned the hose, detached it from the truck, threw it onto the pavement, and told the driver to drive back a bit, in reverse, to reverse. That's what he did, and I tried to run alongside the truck as far as I was able. I was exhausted myself, to tell you the truth. And I just gave him a sign with my hand that he should carry on, continue. I threw myself up against a wall, and underneath Marsal Tito Street there was another Harem that was built in 1993, because there wasn't enough space to bury the dead in the first one. So I lay down on the asphalt there, protected by this wall and some bushes, and when I had caught my breath I continued running with my head down. I ran for another 100 metres, then took a bit of a rest and tried a third time, and I managed to escape the sniper fire. In the meantime, my colleagues came back from the Harem. But while we were doing all this, while all this was going on, detaching the hose and all that kind of thing, there was a man whom I knew by sight. He's an elderly man, a short -- of short build. He jumped off the wall of the Harem, and I said, "Run. You'll be hit again," because I saw that he had already been wounded above his ankle. There was bleeding from the ankle and he'd bandaged up the wound with a handkerchief. He went northwards and we went southwards, and that's how we managed to escape, running alongside the wall. And at Tekija, a little further off -- some 400 metres away is the settlement called Tekija, which was where the out-clinic's patient was -- out-clinic department was, and he went there to get help and he's alive and well today, so the wounding wasn't that serious. And we managed to pull ourselves out. The truck stayed there until the evening, and then we came to tow it away with another truck and all the equipment there. There were about 15 fire extinguishing hoses and all the rest of the equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, sir, is this -- the incident that you told us about just in the last few minutes, is this the incident that is referenced on page 69 of your book, the incident on the 27th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Possibly. Quite possibly. Most probably it is. I can't check that, but, yes, I do know it was July, and I know that we spent a little time wondering what tactics to apply.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: During the time that this was going on, or even when you went to this location, did you know that area to be -- to believe to be or known to be -- at the time to be exposed to sniper fire from a particular location?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: To be quite frank, I did know that it was in that area that there was a sniper's nest, because on several occasions -- well, it wasn't only I myself who knew about that. All of us moving around that area knew about that. That's why I said that I spent a little time to decide whether to go out straight away, because it was risky business. And now, looking at it from this distance in time, I would say that it was madness to go out and try and put out the fire, but I suppose that's what us firemen are like. So I suppose we decided to go out. That's all I can tell you. It was just madness to go out into an open space like that. And the -- you could see everything just like I'm looking at you now. Everything was in full view. But anyway, we went out on this assignment, if nothing else to help the people who had called us in.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you recall, sir, can you tell the Judges the name or give them some reference to this suspected or widely known sniper location? Can you give it a name or some point of reference?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in the briefest possible terms, it was at an elevation by Donja Mahala. Until this damn war, I didn't know that this was called Visnjica or Stotina or whatever. I knew it as Cekak, because as a pupil I would go to that locality where we had some target shooting when I was at school. There was no settlement there. Later on, a rather large settlement was built there. So that was the general area from which they targeted the other parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pejanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: With the assistance of the technical booth, could we please play the video that's marked as Exhibit P09140. 9140. And excuse me. Can I ask the interpreters, please, if they can interpret the B/C/S interpretation because the person there on the scene is speaking into the microphone. That's the part that should be interpreted by the courtroom interpreters, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover]:

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Pejanovic, to the best of your recollection, could you please indicate the location of the fire truck?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. To the best of your recollection, could you please indicate where the firefighters were extinguishing the fire.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. To the best of your recollection, could you please indicate where you were standing when you were shot.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: There.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could you please indicate the direction from where the shots came from?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. To the best of your recollection, could you please indicate where you first saw the old man who was walking towards you and who told you that had been shot at?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now mark with a yellow X the spot where the witness was shot.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Shall I interpret?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Just to make sure there are no misunderstandings, the witness, only the fifth one, was shot and was wounded, none of us were. He did not have anything to do with us. He was the one who was shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, if we can please then go on to the next -- to Exhibit P09139, which again is another 360-degree photograph. We will come back to these other locations in the future, these other aspects in the future. We'll first of all do, again, to orient everyone and the witness, a full revolution. Mr. Pejanovic, you were there at the time that this photograph was being made, as we saw in the other video; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And when the -- the X was marked on the street, you saw that and you'd agree that that was the location, that was the appropriate location?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: As we next -- as we make the next rotation in the photograph, if you can see the Stotina location, the Stotina houses, could you please tell us to stop.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Stop. In the background to the left behind this roof, the spot you have focused on, the spot indicated by the arrow, that is the area concerned. And now we have an even better view.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you indicate -- in reference -- there's a house -- there's an old house or part of a house in the very -- basically, the middle of the photograph, or what appears to be a chimney. Using that as a reference point, can you point the Judges then in the direction of the location that you're referring to as Stotina or the Stotina houses?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: The building that is on fire is a Serbian one which was put -- set on fire in 1992. To the right of that building there is a private house. Could you please rotate the photograph a bit to the -- to the left, and then I will tell you why I want you to do this. A little to the left, please. A little more. Just a little more. Stop. Behind these houses -- behind this house and the hill, since the time of Austro-Hungary, there is a bunker which has been dug in. I've discovered this bunker quite by chance in around 1985 or 1986, I'm not quite sure, though. There was a fire right along this hill and right up to the primary school. In this part -- in this pass, there was a sort of firing range which we would use to train when we were pupils. And in that area, as I have already said, there is a bunker with concrete trenches in very good condition. When we were putting a fire out on one occasion, I discovered this quite by chance. It could have been used to billet units there. And it could have been used as a position from which they could open fire. It's a very safe site. A bunker is almost completely underground and it's made of concrete, and there are also some trenches there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you also show, then, in this photograph, if I can -- in reference to -- again, if you can use the reference point of the chimney, the chimney on the -- the highest chimney there now to the centre left, do you see where the cursor is, the pointer is on the screen?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Okay. In reference to that point, can you again please point out to the Judges the area or location known as Stotina.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: This entire pass is -- bears that name. Up until this cursed war, as I have already said, we called this place Cekek. I wasn't familiar with this other name. It was only in the course of the war that I discovered that two other names were used for this place; Stotina, and Visica [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Where the cursor is now, is this the area that is known as Stotina?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: More or less, because on this slope, as I have already said, there is a bunker. I can claim this with full responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Moving forward, sir. And also in your book, on the 1st of August, 1993, you reference a sniping incident at Musala. Can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, a doctor from Mostar, a gynaecologist, went to collect some water for his house. It's in the immediate vicinity of the square, or to be more precise, in the immediate vicinity of the mosque that is located there. I think he was hit by a sniper as soon as he went out into the street. The former Putnik used to be there, the Putnik company, and I think that Benetton has a site there, or in fact I'm sure that Benetton is located there now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Were you fighting fires in that vicinity on that day, on the 1st of August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: We passed through that area. We passed through that area, and the main problem was to get from our premises to the Musala square. There was an area that was very much exposed to sniper fire, hence the claim that fire could only have been opened from the Privredna Banka, the Privredna bank, because as soon as you set off from the bridge in Musala, you were protected. The former Revija building and the Hotel Bristol protected you. So the sniper had no visibility there. There was only another area where there was -- where things were visible for the sniper, that is if you turned into Adema Buca Street. After you crossed Tito's bridge, it's the first street on the left. He could see you from there but only if he was really waiting for you, then he could hit you. But it was dangerous when we moved from our premises to Tito's bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could you please look at the map again on the ELMO, and place the letter H at the location of this -- the bridge that you referred to now and in connection with the incident you've just told us about.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: With your leave, B1 has been used to mark Tito's bridge, and behind the bridge, at the first crossroads, at the street which is parallel to Santic Street, here we have marked it with B1, that's the street, and the name of the street is Adema Buca.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could you make an H there, please.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Done.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, also in your book you talk about on the 2nd of August, 1993, a shelling of a residential block called Beirut. Can you tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Before we intervened that day, there was some intense shelling that lasted for quite a long time, intense mortar shelling. We were then informed there was a flat on fire in the Beirut block. We had intervened there on a number of occasions because sometimes a shell would fall outside, but it would hit an area where there were a lot of old newspapers and set them on fire. So we had a lot of problems as a result, and we intervened on a number of occasions. But in this case it was a flat that was on fire and we used two vehicles when we intervened. One of the vehicles was a TAM 125 PT-10, which has five cubic -- 1.800 litres of water. And we had a Zastava, which has four cubic metres of water. Since it doesn't have a strong water pump, we used the TAM as the vehicle that could put the fire out. In order to get enough water, in order to get enough water, we poured water from the Zastava into the other vehicle, and then the other vehicle was used to put out the fire in the flat on the fourth floor. The flat was set on fire from the northern side. At that time, there was the driver who was sitting in the Zastava vehicle, and he started looking for a lighter to light a cigarette. Since he couldn't find a lighter, he got out, approached his colleague who was in the entrance to the Beirut building. He approached him. He wanted to light a cigarette, and a new shell fell. But it was really incredible. It was quite by chance that he was there. But it's only thanks to the fact that he couldn't find his lighter and that he couldn't light his cigarette and went to see his colleague that he survived. Otherwise, he would have been torn to pieces. What is even more ironical is that when the vehicle that had been hit and set on fire was taken back by us at night and we tried to check the vehicle to see if we could repair it and get it to function again, believe it or not, on the left side between the gear-shift and the seat we found the lighter, and that was quite fortunate, because if he had found the lighter when he was looking for it, he would have been torn to pieces.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In this particular occasion -- on this particular occasion, sir, just so the record is clear, are you talking about a sniper fire or are you talking about a shell, getting hit by some sort of artillery shell or heavier weapon?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was a mortar shell. That's certain. And quite by chance it fell where it fell. The vehicle was in such a position that he would have been hit if he hadn't gone to light his cigarette by approaching his colleague and by getting out of the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask you once again to look at the map and to mark the location of this incident with the letter I.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Done.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, if I can next direct your attention -- also in your book you mention an incident on the 8th of August, 1993, at Lace Street, number 37.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not quite familiar with this street. I don't think it exists.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I apologise. The full name, I believe, is Hasan Zahirovic Lace Street.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: Zahirovic Lace Street. Yes, that's right. There was a building almost at the bank of the Neretva or, rather, it's about 150 metres from the bank, and the building was also set on fire in the evening -- or, rather, it was just before dawn when we were informed of the fire. We tried to cross over. We tried to get over through a roof so that we could put the fire out from the inside, but as soon as we appeared, as soon as we reached the roof of that building, there was a sniper who was opening fire there. That building was opposite the prison and in the immediate vicinity of the cantonal court. And the post office is there as well as the prison. These facilities are all linked up, so it's quite possible that a sniper opened fire from one of those buildings. The visibility was perfect. I believe he wouldn't even have needed a sniper, he could have used more traditional weapons. So we made a couple of attempts to climb over the roof to put the fire out. The building burnt down. If the owner of the garage or the house had given us access to his garage or house we probably would have been able to do more. Unfortunately, this wasn't the case. We reported matter to the police. I don't know what then happened, because it's not my responsibility to try and receive such information. My responsibility was to intervene in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: On this particular occasion, sir, did you -- if I missed this, I apologise. Were you receiving only rifle fire or were you also -- or were also rocket propelled grenades or RPGs fired at you?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. It was just infantry fire. Infantry weapons were used.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And could we again have on the map, please. Can you show us and mark with the letter J this house that you responded to in order to put out a fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, we have another three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I will finish up, I think, with one or two more questions for now, Your Honour, if I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Pejanovic, can you also mark with the letter K the -- you mentioned a prison a moment ago. Can you mark that location with the letter K.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: The cantonal court was here, and the prison and the post office. Three buildings next to each other. And they're located opposite the building that was on fire. And there's something else I would like to add.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the immediate vicinity the building that was on fire, I believe that there were two civilians who were hit and killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In connection with this particular incident or on another occasion?

utterances.speaker: RATKO PEJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, before this incident, two civilians were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I suggest we stop there. I estimate that I probably have something around 25 minutes or less, I hope. There's one or two additional incident -- final incidents, and then there's some of these incident reports to go through that are marked as exhibits, and a couple final questions, and I hope that altogether it would not take more than approximately 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, because tomorrow the hearing starts at 9.00 and we finish at 1.45. So during that period of time, you'll have to put your outstanding questions to the witness, and the Defence must conduct its cross-examination. If we fail to finish by 1.45, it will be necessary for the witness to stay on until next Monday. I therefore invite the Defence to focus on essential matters, because we have spent an hour on the subject of water, and I fail to see the exact interest of this subject. I can see that Mr. Karnavas is raising his hand. Mr. Karnavas, what would you like to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just four very quick points, Your Honour. First of all, earlier the Prosecution used their programme called Sanction, and I know we're off to a new trial and we're all perhaps a little rusty, but when we go back to the transcript, it's here, there, everywhere being pointed out, nothing marked on an exhibit. So we have this film going back and forth. It will be impossible, I think, at some point to determine where exactly the gentleman is pointing at. I would suggest, and I would urge that in the future if they do intend to use Sanction that they freeze some frames, take some photographs, that way we can have them marked. Otherwise, it makes it very difficult for us to cross-examine on something that was said "here" and "there," and frankly, it's trial advocacy 101. Second of all, the gentleman was in a film and we could see some new buildings. I would appreciate from now on if they would take the trouble to ask the witness first if it's a fair and accurate representation of the scene at the time of the incident. If new buildings have gone up, if the terrain has been changed, we need to know that, especially with respect to what we're talking about, because as a point that was made by General Praljak, and rightly so, at some point we may need to get into a discussion as to the location of these potential snipers. Thirdly, the Prosecution at one point in not doing so out of -- in trying to get edge, in my opinion, but perhaps in trying to speed up the process, used the pointer and in other words was leading the witness and suggesting something to the witness itself. Again, perhaps if they were to provide a picture, then they could ask the witness to point -- to point it out as opposed to the Prosecutor pointing it out to the witness. Then it's the Prosecutor testifying and not the witness. Again, it's their witness, it's direct examination. Finally, and again I apologise, I know we've got to get out of the courtroom, but I'm a little concerned about this new incident that was brought up that's not in the proofing notes. It's nowhere in the disclosure material, and Your Honour Mr. President, you indicated whether it was for context. Now, I must say that it raises a concern, especially if we read the Stakic appeal judgement, and I believe there may be some messages in the Tuta judgement or the Naletilic judgement, appeal judgement that came out yesterday. By that I mean if -- in the Stakic appeal judgement it was very clear that they can use background for context and base that in order to use it for circumstantial evidence to prove a point. Obviously I have to get into that. On this particular occasion, I don't know what I'm going to do, but I certainly don't want that happening in the future. It complicates the situation. If we're trying to truncate this trial, I'm afraid that these sorts of incidents -- and I'm not blaming anyone, but these sorts of incidents will cause us to go into a wider scope than is necessary. And lastly, I want to point out something that Mr. Kovacic did, pointed out earlier with respect to the indictment. The indictment is not quite clear. If you look at Mr. -- Mr. Scott did point out that it goes to April, but then he says -- it's not quite clear. It seems like it is an open-ended. You know, what date is the cut-off date? We need to have some precision. And so these are some thoughts. I apologise to the witness for bringing this up in his presence. I know we've got to be out of here. I tried to keep it in five minutes. Five points; if you could think about it, I would most appreciate it, Mr. President, and thank you for the time. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Kovacic, in a few seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Literally five words. Since you asked us earlier, we were -- at least, couple of counsels were trying to discuss who will ask what on cross this witness during the last break. I don't see there is too much understanding between counsels. Also, because of those reasons. So we will talk more about it, but it easily could be that we will not have our joint plan on dividing the witness on the sections. And after all, the point is that the witness has testified during the direct examination about the time period which is longer than two and half years and about many specific incidents - I guess some 22, at least, if I was not wrong in counting - and besides, this witness was also asked a lot on -- let's say on the context and the events before the conflict between army of BiH and HVO. So that is quite a big territory to go, Your Honour. And I'm not sure we will be able to make agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may, I don't want to contradict my learned colleague and friend Mr. Kovacic, but I can assure you that we're going to do everything we can to make sure that we finish by 1.45 tomorrow, and I'm sure that we can do that provided Mr. Scott stays within that 25, 30-minute ballpark figure that he gave us. I think it can be achieved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you in advance. The hearing will commence tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 5th day of May, 2006, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25
